newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary milling wheat futures down, maize steady.
newsitem.headline: Hungary milling wheat futures down, maize steady.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices dropped on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) while most maize prices, which remained steady on Wednesday, are seen easing, traders said.
"Bleak export prospects and a strong selling side are both exercising downward pressure and I expect a slow easing (of maize prices)," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
He added that four or five market players were likely to start converting their open March positions into later maturities.
Old (1996) crop maize futures prices closed at between 18,800 forints for May and 19,250 for March, while 1997 crop prices ended at between 19,600 for October and 20,600 for December.
Milling wheat prices ended lower for all deliveries by 150 to 400 forints, except for the untraded October maturity, which remained steady.
Wheat futures, however, were likely to remain unpredictable as market players were divided on the size of existing reserves, Monostori said.
"Those who estimate low reserves tend to buy, while the other side would sell," he said.
Tuesday's total turnover was 331.6 million forints or 717 contracts, of which 352 contracts were for maize and 279 for milling wheat.
Both maize and milling wheat only had sizeable turnover for the March delivery.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
